One complete run, no borrowed letters

Bold leans on weight, italic leans on slant, and the run at U+1D468 does both at once in a single set of characters. It is one of the tidier alphabets in the block: fifty-two letters, upper and lower case, all encoded together, with nothing borrowed from an older corner of Unicode. That matters in practice, because the borrowed letters in script and fraktur are the ones that sometimes render a shade off from their neighbours. Here every letter comes from the same run.

It is loud, and that is the point. One word set in bold italic in an otherwise plain listing title, forum post or newsletter subject line reads as the emphasised word without any markup being available. What it cannot do is numbers. There is no bold italic digit set, so any figure you type stays upright and unweighted. If your line is mostly numerals, choose a style that has them.

Also searched as: bold italic text generator, bold italic font copy paste, fancy bold italic letters.

Where Bold Italic text works, and where it does not

WorksWorks in most bios, posts, display names and chat — X, Instagram, TikTok, Discord, Reddit. Watch outRefused by real-name fields (Facebook, LinkedIn's name field) and unsearchable: these are separate characters from ordinary letters, so nobody will find you by typing your name.

Bold Italic questions

How is this different from turning on bold and italic in an editor?

An editor leaves your letters alone and records two attributes about them, which a plain-text field will discard the moment you paste. This generator hands back different characters that were drawn bold and slanted when they were encoded, so the appearance travels with the text into fields that have no formatting.

What happens to my punctuation and spaces?

They pass through untouched. Only the twenty-six upper and twenty-six lower case Latin letters have counterparts in this run, so commas, brackets, spaces and accented letters stay exactly as typed. Numerals stay plain too, since no bold italic digits were ever encoded. Expect a mixed line rather than a uniformly styled one.

Will the styling survive if someone quotes my message?

Usually, because there is nothing to strip: quoting, forwarding and copying all move the characters themselves. What can change is how they look, since that depends on the font on the reader's device rather than on yours. Somebody with incomplete font coverage sees empty rectangles where you see letters.
